headline: Indian Government Healthcare Spending Increases Triple Since 2013
metaDescription: Indian healthcare expenditure reached 4.14 lakh crore in 2023-24, as National Health Accounts data shows a significant drop in out-of-pocket expenses.
aiSummaryBullets: Government healthcare expenditure rose to 4.14 lakh crore in the 2023-24 fiscal year.
Household out-of-pocket medical costs decreased from 64.2% to 42.7% over the last decade.
National Health Accounts reported that social security spending on health grew from 6% to 11%.
aiContextParagraph: According to the National Health Accounts, India has observed a significant shift in its healthcare financing landscape between the 2013-14 and 2023-24 fiscal years. Government health spending has tripled during this period, reaching a total of 4.14 lakh crore. This increase in public funding is reflected in the changing composition of total health expenditure, with the government aiming to reduce the financial burden on individual citizens. Data indicates that the proportion of healthcare costs paid directly by families, known as out-of-pocket expenditure, has declined from 64.2% to 42.7%. Simultaneously, state investment through social security mechanisms has expanded, rising from 6% to 11% of the total health budget. These figures highlight ongoing efforts by national institutions to modify the funding structure of the country's public medical infrastructure and alleviate economic pressure on households for necessary clinical services.
whyItIsViral: The story has gained traction through reports by two major independent national outlets, reflecting significant fiscal updates within the public health sector.
